question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

Nylon was among the first synthitic fibre made by man and is known for its toughness, strength and resistance to oil and grease.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. synthitic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Synthitic" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "synthetic", meaning made by chemical synthesis; artificial, not natural. (कृत्रिम)

◦ Correct: Nylon was among the first synthetic fibres made by man ...

• Spelling key: SYN + THE + TIC (from "synthesis").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "toughness" (the quality of being strong and durable), "strength" (the state of being strong) and "resistance" (the ability to withstand something) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: synthesis (noun), synthesise (verb), synthetic (adjective). Synthetic fibres: nylon, polyester, acrylic, rayon (semi-synthetic); nylon was the first fully synthetic fibre (1935).

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'.

The name, Khajuraho, has probably been derived from the word ‘Khajoor’, meaning date palm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No improvement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Has been derived from" is the correct present perfect passive structure (has/have + been + V3), and the verb "derive" correctly takes the preposition "from" (derived from a source).

◦ Correct: The name, Khajuraho, has probably been derived from the word 'Khajoor' ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "be derived into" and Option 3 "derives into" use the wrong preposition — "derive" pairs with "from", never "into".

• Option 2 "derive at" is unidiomatic; we "arrive at" a conclusion but "derive from" a source.

NOTE

• Passive voice of the present perfect: has/have + been + past participle (has been derived, has been built). Fixed preposition pairs: derive from, originate from, arrive at, result in.

question:
The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

The robbers stabbed him by a sharp knife and he started bleeding profusely on the spot.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. with a sharp knife.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The instrument used to do something takes the preposition "with", not "by". "By" is used for the doer (agent) of the action; "with" is used for the tool/instrument.

◦ Correct: The robbers stabbed him with a sharp knife and he started bleeding profusely on the spot.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly changes the pronoun "him" to "her".

• Option 2 wrongly replaces "and" with "but" — there is no contrast between the two clauses.

• Option 3 "from the spot" is wrong; "on the spot" (immediately/at that very place) is the correct idiom.

NOTE

• Rule: Passive/instrumental use — "He was killed by the robber (agent) with a knife (instrument)." Remember: by + doer, with + instrument.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Tom will _________ the document to the office tomorrow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. mail.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mail" (verb) means to send something by post or electronically. Sending a document to the office requires the verb "mail". (डाक से भेजना)

◦ Correct: Tom will mail the document to the office tomorrow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "mall" (a large shopping centre), Option 2 "meal" (food eaten at one time) and Option 4 "male" (of the masculine sex) are homophone-like words that make no sense in the sentence.

NOTE

• Confusing homophones: mail (post) / male (masculine); meet / meat; week / weak. SSC often tests such similar-sounding words in fill-in-the-blank questions.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

You have spoilt / the little chance you / had at succeeding.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is grammatically correct as it stands: "You have spoilt the little chance you had at succeeding."

◦ "You have spoilt" — correct present perfect (have + V3; "spoilt" is a valid British past participle of "spoil").

◦ "the little chance you" — "little" correctly modifies the uncountable-like sense of "chance", and "you had" is a proper contact (relative) clause with "that/which" understood.

◦ "had at succeeding" — "a chance at + gerund (succeeding)" is an accepted construction, e.g., "a chance at winning".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Spoil" has two correct past forms: spoilt (British) and spoiled (American).

• "Chance" can take "of + gerund", "at + gerund" or "to + infinitive": a chance of succeeding / a chance at succeeding / a chance to succeed.

NOTE

• In "error spotting" questions, do not force an error — if every part follows grammar rules, confidently mark "No error".

question:
Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence.

The vital role played by women at home and in the struggle for freedom, advanced the case for female emancipation soon after the war was over.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. freedom.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Emancipation" means the act of setting free from legal, social or political restrictions; liberation. Its closest synonym is "freedom". (मुक्ति / स्वतंत्रता)

◦ Example: The emancipation/freedom of women gave them equal rights in society.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "bondage" (slavery/captivity) is the antonym of emancipation.

• Option 3 "utility" (usefulness) and Option 4 "objectivity" (impartiality) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of emancipation: freedom, liberation, release, deliverance. Antonyms: bondage, slavery, servitude, subjugation. Related history fact: Abraham Lincoln's "Emancipation Proclamation" (1863) freed slaves in the USA.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

That question is / much difficult / but this one is / very easy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. much difficult.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Much" cannot modify a positive-degree adjective like "difficult". The correct intensifier before a positive adjective is "very" — so it should be "very difficult".

◦ Correct: That question is very difficult but this one is very easy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "That question is", "but this one is" and "very easy" are all correct.

• "Much" is used before a comparative degree: "much more difficult", "much better", "much easier".

NOTE

• Intensifier rule: very + positive degree (very difficult), much + comparative degree (much more difficult). Also: "very" with present participles (very interesting), "much" with past participles (much admired).

question:
Identify the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets.

The magician's performance was (captivating) and held the audience spellbound.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Boring.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Captivating" means holding one's attention completely; charming and fascinating. Its antonym is "boring", meaning dull and uninteresting. (मनमोहक का विलोम — उबाऊ/नीरस)

◦ Example: The captivating show became boring in its second half.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "Fascinating", 3 "Enchanting" and 4 "Gripping" are all synonyms of captivating — a common SSC trap where three options are synonyms and only one is the true antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of captivating: fascinating, enchanting, gripping, mesmerising, spellbinding. Antonyms: boring, dull, tedious, monotonous, unattractive.

question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
option_1: I went to watch a play with one of my friends.
option_2: A famous poet wrote that poem.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. He resides near an university.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The article "an" is used before a vowel sound, not merely a vowel letter. "University" begins with the consonant sound /juː/ ("yoo"), so it takes "a" — "a university".

◦ Correct: He resides near a university.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 correctly uses "one of my friends" (one of + plural noun).

• Options 2 and 3 correctly use the articles "A famous poet" and "A dog".

NOTE

• Article choice depends on sound, not spelling: "a university, a European, a one-rupee note, a useful book" (consonant sounds) but "an hour, an honest man, an MLA, an umbrella" (vowel sounds).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Recieve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Recieve" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "receive", meaning to get or be given something. (प्राप्त करना)

◦ Correct: I receive many letters every week.

• Spelling rule: "i before e, except after c" — after the letter "c", write "ei": re + cei + ve.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Thief", "Believe" and "Relief" are all correctly spelt — in each, "ie" follows a letter other than "c", so "i before e" applies.

NOTE

• Words with "ei" after c: receive, deceive, conceive, perceive, ceiling. Words with "ie": believe, thief, relief, achieve, field. Exceptions to memorise: seize, weird, foreign, height.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I will not be able to ___________ my assignment in time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. complete.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After "to" (the infinitive marker), the base form (V1) of the verb is used — "to complete". The structure is "be able to + V1".

◦ Correct: I will not be able to complete my assignment in time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "completes" (third-person singular), Option 3 "completed" (past form/V2) and Option 4 "completing" (present participle) cannot follow the infinitive "to".

NOTE

• "Be able to + V1" expresses ability (like "can"): "will be able to complete", "was able to finish". Never use V2/V3/V-ing after the infinitive "to" in such structures.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the highlighted word.

His eloquent speech moved the audience to tears.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Expressive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Eloquent" means fluent, forceful and persuasive in speech or writing; effectively expressive. Its closest synonym is "expressive". (वाक्पटु / प्रभावशाली वक्ता)

◦ Example: The leader's eloquent/expressive speech inspired the crowd.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Vernacular" (the local language of a region) is unrelated.

• Option 2 "Inarticulate" (unable to express oneself clearly) is the antonym of eloquent.

• Option 3 "Angry" is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of eloquent: expressive, articulate, fluent, persuasive, silver-tongued. Antonyms: inarticulate, tongue-tied, halting.

question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct.

The grapes taste sweetest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. sweet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Taste" is a linking verb (verb of sensation) and is followed by an adjective in the positive degree when no comparison is made. Since the sentence compares the grapes with nothing, the superlative "sweetest" is wrong — it should simply be "sweet".

◦ Correct: The grapes taste sweet.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "more sweeter" and Option 4 "most sweeter" are double comparatives/superlatives — always incorrect.

• Option 2 "sweeter" (comparative) needs "than" and a second item of comparison, which is absent.

NOTE

• Linking verbs of sensation — taste, smell, look, feel, sound — take an adjective, not an adverb: "The soup tastes good (not well)", "She looks beautiful", "The flowers smell sweet".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The intersection of nature conservation and social justice is evident in efforts to ensure that marginalised communities and other backward classes should have equal access to natural reserves.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. apparent in endeavours to guarantee.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The substitute must keep the same meaning as "evident in efforts to ensure":

◦ "evident" = "apparent" (clearly seen or understood),

◦ "efforts" = "endeavours" (attempts/exertions),

◦ "ensure" = "guarantee" (to make certain).

◦ Correct: ... is apparent in endeavours to guarantee that marginalised communities ... have equal access ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 changes "ensure" to "redesign" (to plan again) — meaning altered.

• Option 2 "Unclear" is the opposite of "evident".

• Option 4 changes "ensure" to "recollect" (to remember) — meaning altered.

NOTE

• Synonym chains useful for SSC: evident–apparent–obvious–manifest; effort–endeavour–attempt–exertion; ensure–guarantee–secure–make certain.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

Her amicable nature made it easy for her to forge positive relationships.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Friendly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Amicable" means having a friendly and pleasant manner; characterised by goodwill. Its closest synonym is "friendly". (मैत्रीपूर्ण / मिलनसार)

◦ Example: Her amicable/friendly nature helped her build positive relationships.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Sad" (unhappy) and Option 4 "Attentive" (paying attention) are unrelated.

• Option 2 "Aggressive" (hostile/forceful) is close to an antonym of amicable.

NOTE

• Synonyms of amicable: friendly, cordial, genial, affable, amiable. Antonyms: hostile, unfriendly, aggressive. Distinguish: amicable (of relations/settlements — an amicable divorce) vs amiable (of a person's nature).

question:
Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank.

The play was shortened by the ___________ of two scenes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. omission.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Omission" means the act of leaving out or excluding something. The play could be shortened only by leaving out (omitting) two scenes. (छोड़ देना / लोप)

◦ Correct: The play was shortened by the omission of two scenes.

• Spelling key: O + MIS + SION (one "m", double "s").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "addition" is correctly spelt but reverses the meaning — adding scenes would lengthen, not shorten, the play.

• Option 3 "ommision" (correct: omission) and Option 4 "insirtion" (correct: insertion) are misspelt.

NOTE

• Word family: omit (verb) – omission (noun) – omitted/omitting (double "t" in inflected forms). Antonyms of omission: addition, inclusion, insertion.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

As 'brutal' is synonymous to 'harsh'

, 'naive' is synonymous to ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. simple.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Naive" means innocent, unsophisticated and lacking worldly experience or judgement. Its closest synonym is "simple". (भोला-भाला / सरल)

◦ Just as brutal = harsh, so naive = simple.

◦ Example: The naive/simple villager believed every word of the trickster.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "wise" (having good judgement) and Option 4 "worldly" (experienced in the ways of the world) are antonyms of naive.

• Option 2 "hospitable" (welcoming to guests) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of naive: simple, innocent, artless, ingenuous, credulous, gullible. Antonyms: worldly, shrewd, sophisticated, experienced.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Hornet's nest
option_4: A house built with great difficulty
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A troublesome or hazardous situation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "hornet's nest" means a very troublesome, dangerous or hazardous situation, especially one that provokes strong angry reactions. To "stir up a hornet's nest" is to create a lot of trouble. (मुसीबत/झंझट भरी स्थिति)

◦ Example: His controversial remark stirred up a hornet's nest in the office.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "A bee's nest" takes the idiom literally — idioms must never be interpreted literally.

• Options 1 and 4 do not convey the sense of provoked trouble.

NOTE

• Related idioms of trouble: "open a can of worms" (create a complicated problem), "in hot water" (in trouble), "add fuel to the fire" (worsen a situation).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The manager complained that Sheetal's email was not up to the standard for the company.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. up to the mark.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "up to the mark" means meeting the required or expected standard. It exactly substitutes "up to the standard". (अपेक्षित स्तर के अनुरूप)

◦ Correct: The manager complained that Sheetal's email was not up to the mark for the company.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "an uphill task" (a very difficult job), Option 3 "up and doing" (busy and active) and Option 4 "under the nose" (right in front of someone) do not fit the sense of "meeting a standard".

NOTE

• Similar expressions: "up to scratch", "up to par", "measure up" — all mean reaching the required standard; "not up to the mark" = below the expected standard.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’.

Mukta requested Nikita to share the picture taken during the wedding.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No improvement required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is already correct: "requested + object + to + V1" is the standard pattern — "Mukta requested Nikita to share the picture ...".

◦ The simple past "requested" suits the completed action, and the participle phrase "taken during the wedding" correctly modifies "the picture".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "will requests" wrongly adds "-s" to the base verb after "will".

• Option 2 "requesting" leaves the sentence without a finite main verb.

• Option 3 "requested Nikita for share" is unidiomatic — "request someone to do something" or "request for something (noun)", never "for share".

NOTE

• Pattern verbs like request/ask/advise/order take: verb + object + to-infinitive — "She asked him to leave", "He advised me to wait".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Saltwater crocodiles are also known as estuarine crocodiles, as they (1)_____________ to live in mangrove-lined rivers. They’re the (2)_________________ living reptile, reaching up to seven metres in length: far larger than Indonesia’s famous Komodo dragon, which tops out at three metres. (3)______________________, crocodiles lived throughout the Indonesian archipelago. We have (4)_________________ of attacks on humans in Bali from the early 20th century and across much of Java until the 1950s. Even Indonesia’s capital, Jakarta, had crocodile’s (5)____________________ in many rivers running through the city.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. prefer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Prefer" means to like one thing/place more than another; to choose by liking. Saltwater crocodiles are called estuarine crocodiles because they prefer (like/choose) to live in mangrove-lined rivers. (पसंद करना)

◦ Correct: ... as they prefer to live in mangrove-lined rivers.

• "Prefer + to-infinitive" (prefer to live) is the correct structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "defer" (to postpone; to yield), Option 2 "refer" (to mention/consult) and Option 3 "differ" (to be unlike) do not fit the sense of habitat choice.

NOTE

• Watch these look-alike verbs: prefer (like better), defer (postpone), refer (mention), differ (disagree/be different), infer (conclude), confer (discuss/bestow).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Saltwater crocodiles are also known as estuarine crocodiles, as they (1)_____________ to live in mangrove-lined rivers. They’re the (2)_________________ living reptile, reaching up to seven metres in length: far larger than Indonesia’s famous Komodo dragon, which tops out at three metres. (3)______________________, crocodiles lived throughout the Indonesian archipelago. We have (4)_________________ of attacks on humans in Bali from the early 20th century and across much of Java until the 1950s. Even Indonesia’s capital, Jakarta, had crocodile’s (5)____________________ in many rivers running through the city.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. largest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clue "reaching up to seven metres in length: far larger than ... Komodo dragon" shows that the passage is talking about size. Hence "the largest living reptile" is correct. (सबसे बड़ा)

◦ Correct: They're the largest living reptile, reaching up to seven metres in length ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fattest" (having most fat), Option 3 "broadest" (widest) and Option 4 "poorest" do not match the comparison of overall size/length.

• The superlative "largest" with "the" is used because the crocodile is compared with all living reptiles.

NOTE

• GK link: the saltwater (estuarine) crocodile is indeed the largest living reptile; the Komodo dragon is the largest living lizard (found in Indonesia).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Saltwater crocodiles are also known as estuarine crocodiles, as they (1)_____________ to live in mangrove-lined rivers. They’re the (2)_________________ living reptile, reaching up to seven metres in length: far larger than Indonesia’s famous Komodo dragon, which tops out at three metres. (3)______________________, crocodiles lived throughout the Indonesian archipelago. We have (4)_________________ of attacks on humans in Bali from the early 20th century and across much of Java until the 1950s. Even Indonesia’s capital, Jakarta, had crocodile’s (5)____________________ in many rivers running through the city.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Historically.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Historically" means in the past; throughout history. The sentence uses the past tense ("crocodiles lived throughout the Indonesian archipelago") and the following lines cite the early 20th century and the 1950s — clearly a historical account. (ऐतिहासिक रूप से)

◦ Correct: Historically, crocodiles lived throughout the Indonesian archipelago.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Abysmally" (extremely badly), Option 3 "Fanatically" (with extreme enthusiasm) and Option 4 "acrobatically" (with gymnastic agility) make no sense as sentence openers here.

NOTE

• Sentence adverbs like Historically, Traditionally, Generally, Interestingly are set off by a comma and comment on the whole sentence.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Saltwater crocodiles are also known as estuarine crocodiles, as they (1)_____________ to live in mangrove-lined rivers. They’re the (2)_________________ living reptile, reaching up to seven metres in length: far larger than Indonesia’s famous Komodo dragon, which tops out at three metres. (3)______________________, crocodiles lived throughout the Indonesian archipelago. We have (4)_________________ of attacks on humans in Bali from the early 20th century and across much of Java until the 1950s. Even Indonesia’s capital, Jakarta, had crocodile’s (5)____________________ in many rivers running through the city.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. records.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Records" means written or documented accounts of past events. We have "records of attacks on humans" — i.e., documented evidence of such attacks from the early 20th century. (अभिलेख / दस्तावेज़)

◦ Correct: We have records of attacks on humans in Bali from the early 20th century ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "recipes" (cooking instructions), Option 3 "regiments" (army units) and Option 4 "residues" (remainders left behind) do not fit documented history.

• "Records of something" is the correct collocation.

NOTE

• "Record" collocations: keep a record, on record, records of attacks/events, record-keeping. Compare: record (noun — document), record (verb — to register).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Saltwater crocodiles are also known as estuarine crocodiles, as they (1)_____________ to live in mangrove-lined rivers. They’re the (2)_________________ living reptile, reaching up to seven metres in length: far larger than Indonesia’s famous Komodo dragon, which tops out at three metres. (3)______________________, crocodiles lived throughout the Indonesian archipelago. We have (4)_________________ of attacks on humans in Bali from the early 20th century and across much of Java until the 1950s. Even Indonesia’s capital, Jakarta, had crocodile’s (5)____________________ in many rivers running through the city.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. residence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Residence" means the place where someone/something lives; dwelling. Jakarta's rivers were places where crocodiles lived — their "residence". (निवास)

◦ Correct: Even Indonesia's capital, Jakarta, had crocodile's residence in many rivers running through the city.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "relevance" (connection with the matter), Option 2 "resistance" (opposition) and Option 4 "remembrance" (memory) do not convey "living/dwelling in the rivers".

NOTE

• Word family: reside (verb — to live), residence (noun — dwelling), resident (noun/adjective — one who lives in a place), residential (adjective — of housing).
